readings.title: The Lĕwite and His Concubine
readings.subtitle: A Journey to Gib‛ah
readings.text: [Judges 19:1] And it came to be in those days, when there was no sovereign in Yisra’ĕl, that there was a certain Lĕwite sojourning in the remote mountains of Ephrayim. And he took for himself a concubine from Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah. [2] And his concubine committed whoring against him, and went away from him to her father’s house at Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah, and was there four months of days. [3] And her husband arose and went after her, to speak to her heart and bring her back, having his servant and a couple of donkeys with him. And she brought him into her father’s house. And the father of the young woman saw him, and rejoiced to meet him. [4] And his father-in-law, the young woman’s father, detained him, and he stayed with him three days. So they ate and drank and spent the night there. [5] And it came to be on the fourth day that they rose early in the morning, and he prepared to go. But the young woman’s father said to his son-in-law, “Refresh your heart with a piece of bread, and afterward go your way.” [6] So they sat down, and the two of them ate and drank together. And the young woman’s father said to the man, “Please agree to stay all night, and let your heart be glad.” [7] And when the man rose to go, his father-in-law urged him, so he spent the night there again. [8] And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go. But the young woman’s father said, “Please refresh your heart.” So they delayed until the day declined, and both of them ate. [9] And when the man rose to go, he and his concubine and his servant, his father-in-law, the young woman’s father, said to him, “See, the day is now drawing toward evening. Please spend the night. See, the day is coming to an end. Stay here, and let your heart be glad. And you shall rise early tomorrow for your journey, and you shall go to your tent.” [10] But the man would not stay that night, but he rose and left, and came opposite Yeḇus, that is Yerushalayim. And with him were the two saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him. [11] They were near Yeḇus and the day had declined, and the servant said to his master, “Come, please, and let us turn aside into this city of the Yeḇusites and spend the night in it.” [12] And his master said to him, “Let us not turn aside here into a city of foreigners, who are not of the children of Yisra’ĕl, but we shall pass over to Gib‛ah.” [13] And he said to his servant, “Come, let us draw near to one of these places, and spend the night in Gib‛ah or in Ramah.” [14] And they passed over and went their way. And the sun went down on them near Gib‛ah, which belongs to Binyamin. [15] And they turned aside there to go in to spend the night in Gib‛ah. And when he went in, he sat down in the open square of the city, for no one took them into his house to spend the night.

readings.title: The Crime at Gib‛ah
readings.subtitle: Wickedness in Binyamin
readings.text: [Judges 19:16] And see, an old man came in from his work in the field at evening, and the man was from the mountains of Ephrayim, and he was sojourning in Gib‛ah. But the men of the place were Binyamites. [17] And he lifted his eyes and saw the traveller in the open square of the city. And the old man said, “Where are you going, and where do you come from?” [18] And he said to him, “We are passing over from Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah toward the remote mountains of Ephrayim. I am from there. And I went to Bĕyth Leḥem in Yehudah, and I am going to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. But there is no one taking me into his house. [19] “Although we have both straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for myself, for your female servant, and for the young man who is with your servant, there is no lack of any matter.” [20] And the old man said, “Peace be with you! However, let all your needs be on me, only do not spend the night in the open square.” [21] And he brought him into his house, and gave fodder to the donkeys. And they washed their feet, and ate and drank. [22] They were making their hearts glad, and see, men of the city, sons of Beliya‛al, surrounded the house, beating on the door. And they spoke to the master of the house, the old man, saying, “Bring out the man who came to your house, so that we know him.” [23] And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, “No, my brothers! I beg you, do no evil! Since this man has come into my house, do not do this folly. [24] “Look, here is my maiden daughter and the man’s concubine. Let me bring them out now. Humble them, and do with them what is good in your eyes, but to this man do not do such a deed of folly.” [25] But the men would not listen to him. So the man took hold of his concubine and brought her out to them. And they knew her and abused her all night until morning, and let her go when the day began to break. [26] And the woman came as the day turned, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her master was, till it was light. [27] And her master rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house and went out to go his way, and saw his concubine fallen at the door of the house with her hands on the threshold. [28] And he said to her, “Rise up and let us go.” But there was no answer. And he took her on the donkey, and the man rose up and went to his place. [29] And when he entered his house he took a knife, and laid hold of his concubine, and cut her according to her bones into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the borders of Yisra’ĕl. [30] And it came to be that all who saw it said, “No such deed has been done or seen from the day that the children of Yisra’ĕl came up from the land of Mitsrayim to this day. Set your heart on it, take counsel, and speak up!”

readings.title: Yisra’ĕl Gathers for War
readings.subtitle: The Assembly at Mitspah
readings.text: [Judges 20:1] Then all the children of Yisra’ĕl came out, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa, as well as the land of Gil‛ad, to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at Mitspah. [2] And the leaders of all the people, all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of <dn>Elohim</dn>, four hundred thousand foot soldiers who drew the sword. [3] And the children of Binyamin heard that the children of Yisra’ĕl had gone up to Mitspah. And the children of Yisra’ĕl said, “Tell us, how did this evil come to be?” [4] And the Lĕwite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, “I came to Gib‛ah that belongs to Binyamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night. [5] “And the masters of Gib‛ah rose against me, and surrounded the house at night because of me. They intended to kill me, but they humbled my concubine so that she died. [6] “So I laid hold of my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the fields of the inheritance of Yisra’ĕl, because they committed a purpose and folly in Yisra’ĕl. [7] “Look, all you children of Yisra’ĕl, give your word and counsel here.” [8] And all the people arose as one man, saying, “Not one of us is going to his tent, nor does any of us turn back to his house, [9] but now this is the deed we do to Gib‛ah: We go up against it by lot! [10] “And we shall take ten men out of every hundred throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl, and a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to make provisions for the people, that when they come to Gib‛ah in Binyamin, they might do to them according to all the folly that they have done in Yisra’ĕl.” [11] So all the men of Yisra’ĕl were gathered against the city, united as one man. [12] And the tribes of Yisra’ĕl sent men through all the tribe of Binyamin, saying, “What is this evil that has been done among you? [13] “And now, give up the men, the sons of Beliya‛al, who are in Gib‛ah, so that we might put them to death and remove evil from Yisra’ĕl.” But the children of Binyamin would not listen to the voice of their brothers, the children of Yisra’ĕl. [14] Instead, the children of Binyamin gathered from the cities to Gib‛ah, to go to battle against the children of Yisra’ĕl. [15] And from the cities on that day the children of Binyamin were numbered at twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gib‛ah, who were numbered at seven hundred chosen men. [16] Among all this people were seven hundred chosen men, left-handed, every one slinging a stone at a hair’s breadth and not missing. [17] And the men of Yisra’ĕl, besides Binyamin, were numbered four hundred thousand men who drew the sword, all of these were men of battle.

readings.title: Civil War Against Binyamin
readings.subtitle: Defeats and Victory
readings.text: [Judges 20:18] And they rose up and went up to the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> and inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the children of Yisra’ĕl said, “Which of us shall go up first to battle against the children of Binyamin?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Yehudah first.”</dq> [19] And the children of Yisra’ĕl rose up in the morning and encamped against Gib‛ah. [20] And the men of Yisra’ĕl went out to battle against Binyamin, and the men of Yisra’ĕl set themselves in battle array to fight against them at Gib‛ah. [21] And the children of Binyamin came out of Gib‛ah, and on that day cut down to the ground twenty-two thousand men of the Yisra’ĕlites. [22] And the people, the men of Yisra’ĕl, strengthened themselves, and again set themselves in battle array in the place where they set themselves in array on the first day. [23] And the children of Yisra’ĕl went up and wept before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> until evening, and asked of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Shall I again draw near for battle against the children of my brother Binyamin?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Go up against him.”</dq> [24] And the children of Yisra’ĕl approached the children of Binyamin on the second day. [25] And Binyamin went out against them from Gib‛ah on the second day, and cut down to the ground eighteen thousand more of the children of Yisra’ĕl, all these drew the sword. [26] And all the children of Yisra’ĕl, that is, all the people, went up and came to the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> and wept, and they sat there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and fasted that day until evening. And they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [27] And the children of Yisra’ĕl asked of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – for the ark of the covenant of <dn>Elohim</dn> was there in those days, [28] and Pineḥas, son of El‛azar, son of Aharon, stood before it in those days – saying, “Shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of my brother Binyamin, or shall I cease?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Go up, for tomorrow <dn>I</dn> give him into your hand.”</dq> [29] And Yisra’ĕl set men in ambush all around Gib‛ah. [30] And the children of Yisra’ĕl went up against the children of Binyamin on the third day, and set themselves in battle array against Gib‛ah as at the other times. [31] And the children of Binyamin went out against the people, and were drawn away from the city. And they began to smite some of the people as at other times, on the highways, one of which goes up to Bĕyth Ěl and the other to Gib‛ah, and in the field, about thirty men of Yisra’ĕl. [32] And the children of Binyamin said, “They are smitten before us as at the first.” But the children of Yisra’ĕl said, “Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways.” [33] And all the men of Yisra’ĕl rose up from their place and set themselves in battle array at Ba‛al Tamar. And the ambush of Yisra’ĕl came forth from their place, from the plain of Geḇa. [34] And ten thousand chosen men from all Yisra’ĕl came against Gib‛ah, and the battle was heavy. But they did not know that evil was coming upon them. [35] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smote Binyamin before Yisra’ĕl. And the children of Yisra’ĕl destroyed that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Binyamin. All these drew the sword. [36] And the children of Binyamin saw that they were smitten. For the men of Yisra’ĕl had given ground to the Binyamites, because they trusted in the ambush which they had set against Gib‛ah. [37] And the ambush hurried and spread out against Gib‛ah. And the ambush moved out and smote all the city with the edge of the sword. [38] Now the appointed signal between the men of Yisra’ĕl and the men in ambush was that they would make a great cloud of smoke rise up from the city, [39] and the men of Yisra’ĕl would turn back in the battle. And Binyamin had begun to smite and kill about thirty of the men of Yisra’ĕl, for they said, “They are certainly smitten before us, as in the first battle.” [40] But when the cloud began to rise from the city in a column of smoke, the Binyamites looked behind them, and see, the whole city was going up in smoke to the heavens! [41] And when the men of Yisra’ĕl turned back, the men of Binyamin were troubled, for they saw that evil had come upon them. [42] And they turned their backs before the men of Yisra’ĕl toward the way of the wilderness. But the battle overtook them, and those who came out of the cities destroyed them in their midst. [43] They surrounded the Binyamites, pursued them, and trod them down as far as the front of Gib‛ah toward the east. [44] And eighteen thousand men of Binyamin fell, all these were men of valour. [45] And they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon. And they gleaned five thousand of them on the highways, and pursued them as far as Gid‛om, and smote two thousand of them. [46] So all who fell of Binyamin that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword, all these were men of valour. [47] But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they dwelt at the rock of Rimmon for four months. [48] And the men of Yisra’ĕl turned back against the children of Binyamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, from the city, men and beasts and all that was found. They also set on fire all the cities they came to.

readings.title: Wives for Binyamin
readings.subtitle: Preserving a Tribe
readings.text: [Judges 21:1] And the men of Yisra’ĕl had sworn an oath at Mitspah, saying, “None of us shall give his daughter to Binyamin as a wife.” [2] And the people came to the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and remained there before <dn>Elohim</dn> till evening. And they lifted up their voices and wept a great weeping, [3] and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl, why has this come to be in Yisra’ĕl, that today there should be one tribe missing in Yisra’ĕl?” [4] And it came to be, on the next day, that the people rose early and built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. [5] And the children of Yisra’ĕl said, “Who is there among all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl who did not come up with the assembly to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” For they had made a great oath concerning anyone who had not come up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at Mitspah, saying, “He shall certainly be put to death.” [6] And the children of Yisra’ĕl had compassion for Binyamin their brother, and said, “One tribe is cut off from Yisra’ĕl today! [7] “What shall we do for wives for those who remain, seeing we have sworn by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that we shall not give them our daughters as wives?” [8] And they said, “What one is there of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl who did not come up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at Mitspah?” And see, no one had come to the camp from Yaḇĕsh Gil‛ad to the assembly. [9] For the people were numbered, and see, not one of the inhabitants of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛ad was there. [10] And the congregation sent twelve thousand of their mighty men of valour there, and commanded them, saying, “Go and smite the inhabitants of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛ad with the edge of the sword, including the women and children. [11] “And this is the word you do: put under the ban every male and every woman who has known a man by lying with him.” [12] And they found among the inhabitants of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛ad four hundred young virgins who had not known a man by lying with him. And they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Kena‛an. [13] And all the congregation sent word to the children of Binyamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them. [14] So Binyamin came back at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive of the women of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛ad. But even so they were not enough for them. [15] And the people had compassion for Binyamin, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had made a breach in the tribes of Yisra’ĕl. [16] And the elders of the congregation said, “What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since the women of Binyamin have been destroyed?” [17] And they said, “There is an inheritance for the survivors of Binyamin, so that a tribe is not blotted out from Yisra’ĕl. [18] “But we are not able to give them wives from our daughters, for the children of Yisra’ĕl have sworn an oath, saying, ‘Cursed be the one who gives a wife to Binyamin.’ ” [19] Then they said, “See, there is a yearly feast of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Shiloh, which is north of Bĕyth Ěl, on the east side of the highway that goes up from Bĕyth Ěl to Sheḵem, and south of Leḇonah.” [20] And they commanded the children of Binyamin, saying, “Go, and lie in wait in the vineyards, [21] “and watch. And see, when the daughters of Shiloh come out to perform their dances, then come out from the vineyards, and every man catch a wife for himself from the daughters of Shiloh. Then go to the land of Binyamin. [22] “And it shall be, when their fathers or their brothers come to us to complain, that we shall say to them, ‘Be kind to them for our sakes, because we did not take a wife for any man in the war, for it is not as though you have given the women to them at this time, making yourselves guilty of your oath.’ ” [23] And the children of Binyamin did so, and they took wives for their number from those who danced, whom they caught. Then they went and returned to their inheritance, and they built the cities and dwelt in them. [24] And at that time the children of Yisra’ĕl went from there, every man to his tribe and to his clan. And they went out from there, every man to his inheritance. [25] In those days there was no sovereign in Yisra’ĕl, everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
